Destinations.title: Destinations
Destinations.description:
Georgia's true uniqueness lies in its extraordinary diversity.

This is a small country where ancient history, breathtaking nature, and a vibrant living culture come together in one remarkable destination. It is here that the earliest Europeans were discovered, on a land that has connected different civilisations for thousands of years while preserving its own unique identity.

Travelling through Georgia means discovering completely different worlds within a single country the timeless peaks of the Caucasus Mountains, the shores of the Black Sea, wild rivers, mysterious caves, dramatic canyons, and landscapes that amaze with their incredible variety.

Yet Georgia's greatest treasure is not only its scenery. It is a country where centuries-old history, unique folklore, polyphonic singing, traditions, culture, and legendary hospitality continue to live and thrive.

Georgia is a place where every region tells its own story, every road leads to a new discovery, and every visitor leaves with a special memory that lasts a lifetime.

tbilisi.name: Tbilisi
tbilisi.lead: Tbilisi a city where centuries of history, diverse cultures, and the rhythm of modern life come together as one unique experience.
tbilisi.p1: Founded in the 5th century around warm sulfur springs, the city was for centuries an important link between East and West. This rich and varied history shaped Tbilisi's distinctive character a place where different eras, cultures, and traditions live side by side.
tbilisi.p2: The narrow streets of Old Tbilisi, houses adorned with wooden balconies, ancient bathhouses, fortress walls, and historic neighborhoods bring the city's past to life, while contemporary architecture, art, cafés, and lively streets create its new energy.
tbilisi.p3: What makes Tbilisi special is its atmosphere here history is not only read in books; it is felt in the streets, flavors, sounds, and the hospitality of the people.

oldTbilisi.name: Old Tbilisi
oldTbilisi.description:
Walking through Old Tbilisi feels like a journey through the city's centuries-old history. It is the place where the past and present of the capital naturally coexist, with every street, courtyard, and traditional balcony preserving stories from different periods of the city's development. It was here that the unique character of Tbilisi was formed a city shaped by the coexistence of different cultures, religions, and traditions.

Cobblestone streets, carved wooden balconies, colourful façades, and historic buildings create the distinctive atmosphere of Old Tbilisi. Within this historic district, visitors can find Orthodox churches, a synagogue, a mosque, and Armenian churches standing close to one another a reflection of the city's multicultural heritage. For centuries, this diversity contributed to Tbilisi's role as an important centre of trade, culture, and social life in the Caucasus.

Today, Old Tbilisi is not only a historical district but also a vibrant part of the modern city, where traditional architecture blends with contemporary life. Charming cafés, wine cellars, local craft workshops, and small galleries add to its unique atmosphere, allowing visitors to experience Tbilisi not only through its landmarks but also through its everyday life.

Exploring Old Tbilisi means discovering the essence of the city a place where history, culture, and local traditions come together to create an unforgettable experience.

narikala.name: Narikala Fortress
narikala.description:
Rising above the historic heart of Tbilisi, Narikala Fortress is one of the city's oldest and most iconic landmarks. For almost 1,700 years, its ancient walls have watched over the capital, witnessing the rise and transformation of a city shaped by different civilisations, cultures, and historical events.

The origins of Narikala date back to the 4th century, when the fortress was first established under the name Shuris-tsikhe as a key defensive stronghold of the Kingdom of Iberia. Over the centuries, it was expanded and strengthened by Georgian rulers, Persians, and Arabs, reflecting the many layers of history that have shaped Tbilisi. Today, Narikala stands as a remarkable reminder of the city's complex and multicultural past.

Built on a strategic hill overlooking the Mtkvari River valley, the fortress once controlled the main routes entering the city and protected one of the most important crossroads between Europe and Asia. Although earthquakes and wars have damaged parts of the original structure, Narikala has remained a powerful symbol of Tbilisi's resilience and enduring spirit.

Today, Narikala offers one of the most spectacular viewpoints in the city. From its walls, visitors can admire sweeping views of Old Tbilisi, the sulphur baths of Abanotubani, the Mtkvari River, the Bridge of Peace, and the modern districts stretching beyond the historic centre. Within the fortress complex stands the restored Church of St. Nicholas, dating back to the 12th-13th centuries, decorated with frescoes inspired by Georgia's religious and historical heritage.

Visiting Narikala is more than exploring an ancient fortress it is an opportunity to see Tbilisi as a living story, where centuries of history unfold in front of your eyes. From this remarkable viewpoint, visitors can understand how the city grew, survived, and became one of the most significant cultural centres of the Caucasus.

Join our tour and discover the centuries-old history of Narikala Fortress, its breathtaking views, and the legends of Tbilisi with a local guide who will bring the stories of this iconic landmark to life.

abanotubani.name: Abanotubani
abanotubani.description:
Located in the heart of Old Tbilisi, Abanotubani is one of the city's oldest and most distinctive historic districts a place where the story of the Georgian capital begins.

According to legend, in the 5th century, King Vakhtang Gorgasali discovered natural hot sulphur springs while hunting in the area. Impressed by the warm waters, he decided to establish a city around them. These springs are believed to have given Tbilisi its name, derived from the Georgian word "tbili", meaning "warm".

Archaeological evidence shows that the sulphur springs were used as early as ancient times, while most of the bathhouses that remain today date back to the 17th-19th centuries. Built with distinctive brick domes and partially set below ground level, these structures reflect the influence of Persian bathhouse architecture and have become one of the most recognisable symbols of Tbilisi.

For centuries, Abanotubani was much more than a place for bathing and relaxation. It served as an important social gathering point where merchants, travellers, writers, and local residents met. The famous French writer Alexandre Dumas visited Tbilisi in the 19th century and described the city's sulphur baths with great admiration in his travel writings.

Today, Abanotubani represents a unique combination of history, architecture, and living tradition. Visitors can explore the historic bathhouses, experience the natural mineral waters, and continue their journey through the nearby landmarks from Narikala Fortress and Leghvtakhevi Waterfall to the narrow streets of Old Tbilisi.

Join our tour and discover the place where the history of Georgia's capital began a district where ancient traditions, remarkable architecture, and the spirit of Tbilisi come together.

metekhi.name: Metekhi Church
metekhi.description:
Rising on a rocky cliff above the left bank of the Mtkvari River, Metekhi Church is one of the most significant historical landmarks of Tbilisi. Its remarkable location overlooking the river, the Old Town, and Narikala Fortress has made it one of the most recognisable symbols of the Georgian capital for centuries.

The history of Metekhi is deeply connected with the origins of Tbilisi itself. According to Georgian historical chronicles, the first church on this site was built in the 5th century by King Vakhtang Gorgasali, the founder of Tbilisi. According to tradition, the royal palace of the Georgian kings was also located here, which is reflected in the name "Metekhi", historically associated with a royal residence or palace area.

The present Metekhi Church mainly dates back to the 13th century and was built during the reign of King Demetre II. At that time, Tbilisi was one of the most important cities in the region, but it was also frequently affected by political conflicts and foreign invasions. Throughout its long history, the church endured destruction, damage, and repeated restoration, becoming a symbol of the city's resilience.

The strategic position of Metekhi was important not only from a religious perspective but also for the defence of Tbilisi. Located on a naturally elevated cliff, the area provided control over the Mtkvari River valley and the historic centre of the city, making it an important part of Tbilisi's defensive system.

Over the centuries, Metekhi witnessed many significant historical events. The church suffered during the Mongol invasions in the 13th century and experienced further hardships during periods of Persian invasions and political instability in the 17th and 18th centuries. In the 19th century, the area was also used for military purposes, while during the Soviet period, preserving the church became an important challenge for maintaining Georgia's cultural heritage.

Metekhi Church is also connected with Georgia's Christian history. According to tradition, the area is associated with Saint Shushanik, one of the earliest Christian martyrs of Georgia. The statue of King Vakhtang Gorgasali standing beside the church further emphasises the connection between this place and the foundation of Tbilisi.

Today, Metekhi Church is not only an important religious and historical monument but also one of the finest viewpoints in the city. From the churchyard, visitors can enjoy a remarkable panorama of Old Tbilisi the Mtkvari River, Narikala Fortress, Abanotubani, and the historic neighbourhoods that define the character of the capital.

Visiting Metekhi Church means discovering a place where the many layers of Tbilisi's history come together from the legends of the city's foundation and the era of Georgian kings to its enduring spiritual and cultural heritage.

Join our tour and discover the centuries-old history, legends, and unique atmosphere of Metekhi Church a place where the story of Tbilisi unfolds before your eyes.

kartlisDeda.name: Mother of Kartli
kartlisDeda.description:
One of Tbilisi's most recognizable symbols, the Mother of Georgia is a monumental statue standing above the city, representing the character of Georgia through the values of hospitality, courage, and love of freedom. Located on the Sololaki Ridge near Narikala Fortress, the monument has been an inseparable part of Tbilisi's skyline for decades.

The statue was created in 1958 by Georgian sculptor Elguja Amashukeli to commemorate the 1,500th anniversary of Tbilisi. Originally made of wood and intended as a temporary structure, the monument gained such symbolic importance that it was decided to preserve it permanently. In 1963, the wooden construction was replaced with the aluminium statue that stands today.

The figure of the Mother of Georgia reflects key elements of Georgian national identity. The sword held in her right hand symbolises the country's readiness to defend itself and protect its freedom, while the wine bowl in her left hand represents Georgia's ancient tradition of hospitality and its welcoming attitude towards guests. Together, these two symbols express the idea that Georgia is a peaceful nation, yet one that has always been prepared to protect its dignity and independence.

The monument's location adds to its significance. From the Mother of Georgia, visitors can enjoy one of the most impressive views over Tbilisi the historic Old Town, the Mtkvari River valley, modern districts, and the surrounding mountains. For this reason, it has become one of the city's most popular viewpoints and an essential stop for those wishing to understand both the history and character of the Georgian capital.

Today, the Mother of Georgia is more than just a statue it is a symbol of Tbilisi's identity and one of the first landmarks associated with Georgia's capital by visitors from around the world. A visit here offers a deeper understanding of the country's historical experience, cultural values, and the unique relationship Georgians have with both their homeland and their guests.

Join our tour and discover the iconic symbols of Tbilisi. With stories shared by a local guide, learn what the Mother of Georgia reveals about the country's history, traditions, and national character.

rikeParkPeaceBridge.name: Rike Park & Peace Bridge
rikeParkPeaceBridge.description:
Rike Park is one of Tbilisi's most distinctive contemporary public spaces, where the historic atmosphere of the Old Town meets modern urban design. Located on the left bank of the Mtkvari River in the heart of the city, the park has become one of the capital's most popular places for relaxation and leisurely walks, offering remarkable views of Narikala Fortress, Metekhi Church, and the historic neighbourhoods of Old Tbilisi.

The area known today as Rike has been an important part of Tbilisi's urban landscape for centuries. The Georgian word "Rike" refers to a low, sandy riverside area formed by the movement of the river. In the past, this part of the city had a very different appearance it was associated with trade, crafts, and everyday riverside activities, playing an important role in the social and economic life of Tbilisi. Over time, the area was transformed, and in the 21st century it became one of the city's most recognisable modern public spaces.

Officially renovated in 2010, Rike Park became one of the symbols of Tbilisi's contemporary development. Its open green areas, walking paths, fountains, and recreational spaces create a welcoming environment for both residents and visitors. The park is especially atmospheric in the evening, when illuminated pathways and views of the historic city create a unique contrast between Tbilisi's past and present.

One of the park's most prominent landmarks is the Bridge of Peace, which connects Rike Park with the historic district on the opposite side of the Mtkvari River. Opened in 2010, the bridge's distinctive glass and steel structure has become one of the most recognisable examples of modern architecture in Tbilisi. Stretching across the river, it serves as both a functional connection and a symbolic link between the city's historic heritage and its contemporary identity.

Rike Park is also an important starting point for exploring some of Tbilisi's most significant attractions, including the Old Town, Abanotubani sulphur baths, and Narikala Fortress. From here, visitors can experience the remarkable contrast between medieval architecture, the flowing river landscape, and the modern face of the capital.

The true significance of Rike Park lies in its ability to unite two different sides of Tbilisi a city with centuries of history and a capital continuously evolving with the modern world. It is a place where visitors can admire ancient landmarks, enjoy the riverside atmosphere, and experience the changing identity of contemporary Tbilisi.

Join our tour and discover the place where Tbilisi's historic heritage and modern identity come together explore Rike Park, cross the Bridge of Peace, and uncover the stories behind the city's transformation with a local guide.

mtatsminda.name: Mtatsminda
mtatsminda.description:
Mtatsminda is one of the most distinctive landmarks of Tbilisi, where nature, history, culture, and breathtaking city views come together in one remarkable place. Rising above the capital, this mountain has been an inseparable part of Tbilisi's identity for centuries and remains one of the city's most beloved destinations for both locals and visitors.

The name "Mtatsminda" means "Holy Mountain" in Georgian and reflects the site's deep historical and spiritual significance. On the slopes of the mountain stands the Church of St. David, associated with Saint David Garejeli, one of the thirteen Assyrian Fathers who arrived in Georgia in the 6th century to strengthen Christian traditions in the country. Over time, this area became an important religious centre, and Mtatsminda developed into a place of spiritual reflection and special cultural importance for the people of Tbilisi.

In the 19th century, Mtatsminda gained a new role as one of the city's important cultural spaces. The development of the mountain began in the 1850s, and in 1859 the Mtatsminda Pantheon was established a historic cemetery where many of Georgia's most prominent writers, artists, and public figures are buried. Among them are Ilia Chavchavadze, Akaki Tsereteli, and Nikoloz Baratashvili, whose contributions shaped Georgian literature, culture, and national identity. Today, the Pantheon remains one of the country's most important sites of cultural memory.

Mtatsminda became even more closely associated with Tbilisi's identity in the 20th century, with the opening of Mtatsminda Park and the construction of the city's famous funicular railway. The Tbilisi Funicular began operating in 1905 and has remained one of the capital's most recognisable landmarks. The journey itself is part of the experience as the funicular climbs the mountain, visitors gradually leave behind the rhythm of the city and ascend towards one of the finest viewpoints in Tbilisi.

From Mtatsminda Park, visitors can enjoy a spectacular panorama of the capital, with views stretching across Old Tbilisi, the Mtkvari River valley, Narikala Fortress, the Mother of Georgia, and the modern districts of the city. The location is especially popular at sunset, when Tbilisi begins to glow with evening lights and reveals a completely different atmosphere.

Today, Mtatsminda is much more than a recreational destination. It is a place where the history, cultural heritage, and modern life of Tbilisi come together. Visiting this mountain means not only enjoying some of the city's most impressive views but also discovering a place that has played an important role in shaping the identity of the Georgian capital.

Join our tour and discover the history of Mtatsminda, the legends of the funicular, and the most spectacular views of Tbilisi through the stories shared by a local guide.

botanicalGarden.name: Tbilisi Botanical Garden & Leghvtakhevi Waterfall
botanicalGarden.description:
The Tbilisi Botanical Garden and Leghvtakhevi Waterfall are among the rare places where the centuries-old history of the city and the beauty of nature exist in remarkable harmony. Located in the heart of Old Tbilisi, near Narikala Fortress, this unique area allows visitors to leave behind the rhythm of the city within minutes and enter a peaceful green valley where nature, history, and landscape come together as one unforgettable experience.

The history of the Botanical Garden dates back to the 18th century. The area was originally connected with the gardens of the Tbilisi Fortress and royal gardens, while the Tbilisi Botanical Garden was officially established in 1845. During the 19th century, it became one of the leading centres for the study and preservation of plant species in the Caucasus region. Its unique location along the Mtkvari River valley and the slopes of the Sololaki Ridge creates a special microclimate, allowing the garden to preserve a remarkable variety of flora from different regions of Georgia and around the world.

Today, the Tbilisi Botanical Garden covers approximately 160 hectares and offers visitors a diverse natural environment with rare plant species, scenic landscapes, historic bridges, and peaceful walking paths. Its charm lies not only in its scientific importance but also in its role as a place for relaxation, exploration, and discovering the greener side of Tbilisi.

One of the most impressive parts of the garden is Leghvtakhevi Waterfall, considered one of the most unexpected natural discoveries in the historic centre of Tbilisi. The name "Leghvtakhevi" is associated with fig trees that traditionally grew in this valley. For centuries, this area formed a natural extension of the old neighbourhoods of Tbilisi, and today it has become one of the city's most popular walking routes.

A walk through the narrow Leghvtakhevi gorge offers a truly unique experience. Ancient stone walls, lush vegetation, small bridges, and the sound of flowing water create a peaceful atmosphere just steps away from the historic streets of Old Tbilisi. Rising approximately 22 metres, the waterfall is one of the most remarkable natural landmarks located within the city centre.

The Tbilisi Botanical Garden and Leghvtakhevi Waterfall represent the elements that make Tbilisi such a distinctive city ancient history, diverse culture, and nature that remains alive even within an urban environment. It is a place where visitors do not simply observe the city, but discover a quieter, more authentic side of its character.

Join our tour and discover one of Tbilisi's hidden natural treasures walk through the Leghvtakhevi gorge, explore the Botanical Garden, and uncover the stories that have shaped this unique place over centuries.

chronicleMonument.name: Chronicle of Georgia
chronicleMonument.description:
The Chronicle of Georgia, often referred to as the "Chronicle Monument", is one of Tbilisi's most impressive yet lesser-known landmarks. Rising on a hill near the Tbilisi Sea, this monumental artwork presents the history of Georgia on a grand scale, combining sculpture, architecture, and storytelling into a single remarkable space. Due to its enormous size and dramatic appearance, it is sometimes described as the "Georgian Stonehenge".

The creation of the monument began in 1985 by the renowned Georgian sculptor and artist Zurab Tsereteli. Although the ambitious project has never been fully completed, its scale, artistic vision, and cultural significance have made it one of the most unique landmarks in Tbilisi.

The Chronicle of Georgia consists of around 16 massive columns, reaching approximately 30-35 metres in height. The granite and bronze reliefs carved into the monument depict key chapters of Georgian history the adoption of Christianity, the life and mission of Saint Nino, Georgian kings and queens, historic battles, important cultural and literary figures, as well as biblical scenes. Each panel serves as a visual historical record, bringing together different eras of Georgia's past within one monumental composition.

Among the most striking elements of the monument are the depictions of Georgian rulers, reflecting the country's long tradition of statehood and royal heritage. A significant part of the artwork is dedicated to Christian themes, highlighting the important role of Orthodox Christianity in shaping Georgia's cultural identity and historical development.

The monument's location adds greatly to its atmosphere. Standing above the Tbilisi Sea, it offers wide panoramic views over the city, the reservoir, and the surrounding landscapes. The site is especially impressive at sunset, when the massive columns and detailed reliefs are illuminated by golden light, creating a dramatic and unforgettable scene.

Unlike the historic streets, medieval churches, and traditional architecture found in other parts of Tbilisi, the Chronicle of Georgia represents a modern interpretation of national memory an attempt to preserve and express the story of an entire nation through monumental art.

Visiting the Chronicle of Georgia offers an opportunity to discover Georgia not only as a country, but as a civilisation shaped by its rulers, faith, struggles, artistic achievements, and centuries-old cultural heritage.

Join our tour and discover Georgia's history carved in stone visit a monumental artwork that brings together the nation's past, cultural heritage, and one of the most impressive viewpoints of Tbilisi.

gudiashviliSquare.name: Lado Gudiashvili Square
gudiashviliSquare.description:
Stepping into Lado Gudiashvili Square feels like a journey into the atmosphere of Old Tbilisi a place where centuries of history, traditional architecture, and the city's creative spirit come together in one intimate yet remarkable space. Located near Freedom Square, the square is one of the rare places where the historic character of Tbilisi has been carefully preserved, allowing visitors to experience the authentic atmosphere of the old city.

The history of the square stretches back approximately 600 years. It first appeared on Tbilisi's city plan in 1785, during the reign of King Erekle II. Throughout different periods, the square was known by several names, including Bejanas Baghi, Abbas-Abad Square, Kolortaghi, Alaverdov, and later Moghnis Square. Each name reflects a different chapter of the area's diverse and complex history.

The unique charm of Lado Gudiashvili Square lies in its preserved Old Tbilisi architecture 19th-century buildings, traditional wooden balconies, brick cellars, and a mixture of architectural influences from different eras. One of the most notable buildings on the square is an early 19th-century residential house, locally known as the "Blue House". Throughout its history, the building served various purposes, including housing offices of the Russian Imperial military administration and later the editorial office of the newspaper "Literary Georgia". The building is also connected with the visit of the Russian poet Mikhail Lermontov to Tbilisi in 1838.

The square also holds a special connection with Georgian art and culture. It was once a gathering place for Tbilisi's creative circles, and today it carries the name of the renowned Georgian artist Lado Gudiashvili (1896-1980). His work was deeply inspired by the people, streets, and everyday life of Old Tbilisi, capturing the unique character of the city and its inhabitants.

A major restoration project began in 2018 with the aim of preserving the historic identity of the square and restoring the original appearance of its buildings. The project focused on the careful restoration of façades, preservation of historic cellars, and protection of important architectural details.

Today, Lado Gudiashvili Square is one of the most charming and atmospheric corners of Tbilisi. Visitors do not simply see a beautiful historic square they discover the different layers of the city itself: the structure of old neighbourhoods, 19th-century Tbilisian architecture, the artistic heritage of the 20th century, and the rhythm of contemporary urban life.

Join our tour and uncover the hidden stories of Old Tbilisi walk through Lado Gudiashvili Square, where architecture, art, and centuries of the city's memory come together in one remarkable place.

sameba.name: Holy Trinity Cathedral
sameba.description:
The Holy Trinity Cathedral of Tbilisi, widely known as Sameba, is one of the most significant symbols of modern Georgia. Rising above the city with its monumental golden dome, the cathedral represents the country's spiritual heritage, cultural identity, and renewed national confidence. Located on the hill of Saint Elijah on the left bank of the Mtkvari River, Sameba has become one of the most impressive landmarks of the Georgian capital.

The construction of Holy Trinity Cathedral began in 1995 with the aim of creating a symbol of the revival of the Georgian Orthodox Church and a landmark representing the new era of independent Georgia. The cathedral was officially consecrated on 23 November 2004, on the Georgian Orthodox celebration of Giorgoba (the Feast of Saint George). Its construction was dedicated to two major historical milestones the 1,500th anniversary of the restoration of the autocephaly of the Georgian Orthodox Church and the 2,000th anniversary of Christianity in Georgia.

Designed by Georgian architect Archil Mindiashvili, the cathedral is based on the principles of traditional Georgian ecclesiastical architecture while expressing the scale and ambition of the modern era. With a height of approximately 87 metres, including the cross, Sameba is one of the tallest religious buildings in Georgia and one of the largest Orthodox cathedrals in the world.

The Holy Trinity Cathedral complex extends far beyond the main church building. Its territory includes several smaller churches, a bell tower, religious and administrative buildings, gardens, and underground spaces. The interior is distinguished by its impressive scale, traditional Georgian decorative elements, and examples of contemporary iconography, making it an important centre of modern Georgian religious art.

Sameba holds significance not only as a place of worship but also as a symbol of national unity and cultural revival. Built during the period of independent Georgia, the cathedral represents the connection between the country's historical heritage, spiritual traditions, and modern identity.

The location of the cathedral creates an additional visual experience. From its courtyard, visitors can enjoy panoramic views over Tbilisi, including the historic neighbourhoods and modern districts of the city. The cathedral is especially striking in the evening, when its illuminated golden dome becomes one of the most prominent features of the Tbilisi skyline.

Visiting Holy Trinity Cathedral is more than experiencing an architectural landmark it offers an opportunity to understand contemporary Georgia, its Orthodox traditions, and the national symbol that has become an inseparable part of Tbilisi's identity.

Join our tour and discover the spiritual centre of Tbilisi explore the history, architecture, and significance of Sameba Cathedral through the stories shared by a local guide.

meidanBazaar.name: Meidan Bazaar
meidanBazaar.description:
Meidan Bazaar is one of the most authentic and atmospheric corners of Old Tbilisi, where the city's centuries-old tradition of trade, craftsmanship, and cultural exchange comes to life. Located in the historic heart of the capital, near Abanotubani and the old Meidan Square, this unique space reveals the story of Tbilisi as a city that for centuries connected different worlds along the crossroads between Europe and Asia.

The name "Meidan" originates from the Persian word meydan, meaning "square" or "open gathering place". Throughout history, this area served as one of the most important public spaces of Old Tbilisi, where merchants, travellers, artisans, and representatives of different cultures met and exchanged goods, ideas, and traditions. Its location along major trade routes helped Tbilisi develop into a multicultural centre, and Meidan became one of the city's most vibrant meeting points.

For centuries, the area surrounding Meidan was known for its caravanserais, workshops, and traditional trading houses. Merchants arriving from distant regions would store their goods here, rest during their journeys, and participate in the economic and social life of the city. This diverse atmosphere shaped the unique identity of Tbilis a city where Georgian traditions blended with influences from the wider world.

Today, Meidan Bazaar preserves the spirit of the historic marketplace within a beautifully restored underground space. Traditional brick arches, stone walls, and intimate passages create an atmosphere reminiscent of old caravanserais and centuries-old trading quarters. Visitors can discover Georgian wine, handmade crafts, traditional sweets, spices, souvenirs, and authentic products reflecting the country's culture and traditions.

The significance of Meidan Bazaar goes far beyond shopping. It offers travellers a direct connection with Georgian everyday life a place to explore the country's ancient winemaking traditions, taste local flavours, discover traditional craftsmanship, and take home a piece of Georgia's cultural heritage.

Its location makes Meidan Bazaar an ideal starting point for exploring Old Tbilisi. Within walking distance are some of the city's most important landmarks, including the Abanotubani sulphur baths, Narikala Fortress, Leghvtakhevi Waterfall, and the charming historic streets of the old district.

Visiting Meidan Bazaar means experiencing one of the essential elements of Tbilisi's character a city shaped by trade, cultural encounters, and centuries of shared history.

Join our tour and discover the trading heritage of Old Tbilisi explore historic Meidan, experience the atmosphere of the traditional bazaar, and uncover the stories, flavours, and traditions that have shaped the city for centuries.

dryBridgeMarket.name: Dry Bridge Market
dryBridgeMarket.description:
Dry Bridge Market is one of the most unique and authentic experiences in Tbilisi, where the city's past continues to live through thousands of objects, old photographs, artworks, and personal belongings. Here, ordinary items become extraordinary stories antique clocks, books, jewellery, paintings, coins, and household objects reveal memories of different people, eras, and the changing face of the city.

The market is located near the historic Dry Bridge, whose origins date back to the late 19th century. Originally, the bridge crossed one of the branches of the Mtkvari River; however, after changes to the river landscape, this section dried up, giving the bridge its unusual name the "Dry Bridge".

The history of the market is closely connected with the 1990s, a challenging period in Georgia's recent history following the collapse of the Soviet Union. During this time, many people began selling personal possessions, gradually transforming the area into the unique open-air marketplace that attracts visitors from around the world today.

Nowadays, Dry Bridge Market is considered one of the most famous antique and art markets in the region. Visitors can discover Soviet-era collectibles, vintage cameras, vinyl records, handmade jewellery, traditional Georgian artworks, paintings, and countless objects representing different layers of Georgia's cultural history.

The true charm of the market lies in its unpredictability you never know what discovery awaits at the next table. It may be a 19th-century book, an old photograph of Tbilisi, a painting by a Georgian artist, or simply an everyday object carrying a personal story that has been preserved through generations.

Dry Bridge is also an important gathering place for artists and craftspeople. Local painters, artisans, and collectors regularly present their works here, making the market not only a place of trade but also a living part of Tbilisi's creative culture.

Visiting Dry Bridge Market means discovering the city through its everyday life and personal memories. It is not a museum behind glass it is a living space where history unfolds directly in front of you, and every object has a story waiting to be discovered.

Join our tour and uncover the hidden stories of Tbilisi explore Dry Bridge Market, meet local collectors, and discover unique objects that preserve the memories of Georgia's past.

clockTower.name: Rezo Gabriadze Clock Tower
clockTower.description:
Hidden among the narrow streets of Old Tbilisi, the Rezo Gabriadze Clock Tower is one of the city's most distinctive and enchanting landmarks. A place where art, theatre, and the unique spirit of Tbilisi come together, the tower feels as though it has stepped directly out of a fairytale and found its home among the historic streets of the old city.

The tower was created by the renowned Georgian artist, writer, director, and founder of the Marionette Theatre, Rezo Gabriadze. Completed in 2010, it became part of the complex surrounding the Rezo Gabriadze Marionette Theatre. Although relatively new compared to Tbilisi's ancient monuments, the tower quickly became one of the city's most recognisable symbols.

Its charm lies in its unconventional architecture. The structure appears to be assembled from fragments of different eras small balconies, leaning walls, painted doors, and handmade ceramic details create a unique visual world that perfectly reflects Gabriadze's artistic imagination. The decorative ceramic tiles adorning the tower were personally designed by the artist, giving the building a deeply personal and artistic character.

The tower's most beloved feature is its small clock and mechanical performance. Every hour, an angel appears from behind a decorated door and gently rings a bell with a small hammer. Twice a day, at 12:00 and 19:00, visitors can witness the short mechanical performance "The Circle of Life", a symbolic story about love, family, and the journey of human life.

What makes the Rezo Gabriadze Clock Tower truly special is that it does not simply imitate the atmosphere of Old Tbilisi it has become a natural part of the old city itself. The tower combines Georgian theatrical traditions, handmade artistry, and one of Tbilisi's most distinctive qualities: the ability to place deep history and gentle humour side by side.

Today, the clock tower is one of the most photographed and beloved landmarks in Tbilisi. Visitors come not only to admire its unusual architecture but also to experience the feeling it creates the sense that there are still places in the city where imagination, creativity, and art can transform everyday life.

Join our tour and discover one of Tbilisi's most magical corners explore Rezo Gabriadze's creative world, uncover the stories behind the clock tower, and experience the unique atmosphere that makes this place unforgettable.

sionCathedral.name: Sioni Cathedral
sionCathedral.description:
Sioni Cathedral is one of the oldest and most significant historical monuments in Tbilisi, representing the spiritual and cultural heart of the city for centuries. Located in the centre of Old Tbilisi near the right bank of the Mtkvari River, the cathedral is not only an important religious site but also a witness to many of the defining moments of Georgia's history.

The history of Sioni Cathedral dates back to the early medieval period. According to historical sources, the first church on this site was likely built in the 6th-7th centuries. However, due to repeated invasions, wars, and destruction throughout the centuries, the cathedral was rebuilt several times. The main appearance of the present structure is largely connected with restorations carried out in the 13th century, when Tbilisi was one of the most important political and cultural centres of the Georgian Kingdom.

The name "Sioni" is connected with Mount Zion in Jerusalem, carrying deep symbolic meaning within Georgian Christian tradition. For centuries, Sioni served as the seat of the Catholicos-Patriarch of Georgia and was the place where many of the country's most important religious ceremonies and events took place.

The cathedral holds particular spiritual significance due to its connection with one of the most important relics of Georgian Christianity the vine cross associated with Saint Nino. According to Georgian tradition, Saint Nino played a central role in bringing Christianity to Georgia in the 4th century. Today, Sioni remains closely connected with this important chapter of the country's religious heritage.

Architecturally, Sioni Cathedral is a remarkable example of traditional Georgian ecclesiastical design. Built according to the principles of Georgian cross-dome architecture, the cathedral is distinguished by its stone façade, harmonious proportions, and powerful historical atmosphere. Inside, visitors can discover significant examples of Georgian iconography and religious art.

The uniqueness of Sioni also comes from its location in the very heart of the historic area where everyday life in Tbilisi developed over centuries. Surrounding the cathedral are some of the city's most important landmarks, including Meidan Square, Anchiskhati Basilica, Abanotubani, and the route towards Narikala Fortress together forming the ancient core of Tbilisi.

Today, Sioni Cathedral remains both an active place of worship and an important part of Georgia's cultural memory. Visiting this sacred site offers an opportunity to connect with the era when Tbilisi was not only a city but also a major political, commercial, and spiritual centre of the Caucasus.

Join our tour and discover the historic heart of Tbilisi visit Sioni Cathedral, uncover its centuries-old stories, and experience a place where Georgia's spiritual heritage continues to live.

nationalMuseum.name: Georgian National Museum
nationalMuseum.description:
The Georgian National Museum is a place where thousands of years of Georgia's history come together in one remarkable space from the earliest traces of human life and the golden treasures of ancient Colchis to medieval Christian art and the story of modern Georgia.

Located on Rustaveli Avenue in the centre of Tbilisi, the museum is one of the country's most important cultural institutions. It brings together some of Georgia's most valuable collections of archaeology, history, ethnography, and art, offering visitors a deeper understanding of the nation's remarkable heritage.

The true significance of the museum lies in the fact that it allows visitors to discover Georgia not simply as a modern country, but as an ancient civilisation shaped over thousands of years. Its collections include prehistoric archaeological discoveries, ancient gold and silver artefacts, Christian artworks, coins, manuscripts, and ethnographic treasures that reveal the richness of Georgia's cultural development.

One of the museum's most remarkable highlights is the collection of Colchian gold, which demonstrates the advanced craftsmanship and cultural achievements of ancient Georgia. Another exceptional part of the collection is connected with the archaeological discoveries of Dmanisi, where some of the earliest human remains outside Africa were found, placing Georgia among the most important sites in global palaeoanthropological research.

For those interested in Georgian history, the archaeological exhibitions provide a fascinating journey through different eras from the Stone Age and Bronze Age to the ancient kingdoms, medieval period, and beyond. These collections reveal Georgia's long-standing role as a meeting point of cultures and civilisations in the Caucasus.

A visit to the Georgian National Museum is especially valuable for travellers who want to understand the deeper meaning behind the landmarks they encounter throughout Tbilisi. Narikala Fortress, Sioni Cathedral, Anchiskhati Basilica, Sameba Cathedral, and the streets of Old Tbilisi become more than individual attractions they become part of a much larger historical story.

The Georgian National Museum is the perfect starting point for anyone who wants to understand what Georgia truly represents not only as a country, but as a civilisation with a unique and enduring cultural legacy.

Join our tour and discover the greatest treasures of Georgian history travel through thousands of years of civilisation and explore the country's heritage through its most remarkable collections.

historicEntrances.name: Historic entrances of Tbilisi
historicEntrances.description:
One of Tbilisi's most hidden and unique treasures can be found behind the old wooden doors of its historic residential buildings. While walking through the streets of the old districts, visitors often discover unexpected architectural gems elegant entrances decorated with painted walls, colourful stained-glass windows, ornamental ceilings, marble floors, and artistic details that reveal the city's rich cultural past.

At the end of the 19th and beginning of the 20th centuries, Tbilisi experienced rapid development and became one of the most important commercial and cultural centres of the Caucasus. During this period, many impressive residential buildings were constructed, and their entrances were designed not only as functional spaces but also as a reflection of the owner's social status, taste, and cultural influence.

The uniqueness of Tbilisi's historic entrances lies in their remarkable diversity. Here, European architectural influences blend with Eastern decorative traditions and the distinctive character of old Tbilisi. Some buildings feature Art Nouveau elements, hand-painted ceilings, colourful stained-glass windows, carved wooden staircases, and beautifully designed mosaic floors.

The neighbourhoods of Sololaki, Mtatsminda, Vera, and Chugureti are especially famous for preserving some of the finest examples of late 19th and early 20th-century residential architecture. Hidden behind ordinary street façades are interiors that tell stories of a different era a time when architecture was closely connected with art and everyday life.

Among the most remarkable examples are:

Historic houses on Galaktion Tabidze Street - known for their decorative interiors, painted walls, and elegant architectural details;

The entrances of Ivane Machabeli Street - reflecting the refined lifestyle and atmosphere of old Tbilisi's cultural elite;

Historic buildings on Lado Asatiani Street - preserving authentic elements of traditional Tbilisi interiors.

What makes these entrances truly special is that they are not preserved as museum exhibits people still live in these buildings today. This creates a unique atmosphere where history is not separated from everyday life but continues to exist naturally alongside modern Tbilisi.

Discovering Tbilisi's historic entrances means experiencing another side of the city not only its famous monuments and landmarks, but also the homes, stories, and lifestyles of the people who shaped its identity.

Join our tour and uncover Tbilisi's hidden architectural treasures open the old doors of the city and discover the stories that remain invisible from the streets.

guria.name: Guria
guria.lead: Georgia's Hidden Land of Tea, Wine & Authentic Traditions
guria.p1: Far beyond Georgia's well-known tourist destinations lies Guria a region where life moves at a slower pace, traditions remain untouched, and every journey becomes a genuine cultural experience.
guria.p2: Nestled between the Black Sea coast and the Lesser Caucasus Mountains, Guria is a land of rolling tea plantations, rare endemic grape varieties, family wineries, mountain villages, and warm local hospitality.
guria.p3:
Unlike the country's more famous wine regions, Guria invites travelers to discover Georgia through intimate encounters: sharing homemade wine with local winemakers, tasting artisan cheeses on family farms, exploring historic tea plantations, meeting traditional qvevri makers, and experiencing a way of life that has remained authentic for generations.

Whether you are passionate about gastronomy, wine, tea, nature or cultural heritage, Guria offers one of the most rewarding off-the-beaten-path experiences in Georgia.

gomismta.name: Gomismta
gomismta.description:
Nestled at more than 2,000 meters above sea level in the Lesser Caucasus Mountains, Gomismta is one of Georgia's most breathtaking summer mountain resorts and one of Guria's true hidden gems. Famous for its spectacular "Sea of Clouds," this remote alpine destination offers visitors an unforgettable experience where mountain peaks rise above a blanket of clouds, creating one of the country's most iconic natural landscapes.

Unlike many popular tourist destinations, Gomismta has preserved its peaceful and authentic character. Traditional wooden cottages, lush alpine meadows, crystal-clear mountain springs, and endless panoramic views create the perfect setting for travelers seeking tranquility, nature, and fresh mountain air. During the summer months, the region becomes a paradise for hikers, photographers, outdoor enthusiasts, and anyone looking to escape the heat of the lowlands.

One of Gomismta's greatest attractions is sunrise and sunset, when the clouds slowly drift through the valleys below, transforming the landscape into an ever-changing natural spectacle. Visitors can enjoy scenic hiking trails, horseback riding, picnics surrounded by alpine flowers, and breathtaking viewpoints overlooking the Gurian mountains.

Whether you are searching for adventure, relaxation, or simply one of Georgia's most unforgettable landscapes, Gomismta promises an authentic mountain experience far from the usual tourist routes.

bakhmaro.name: Bakhmaro
bakhmaro.description:
Hidden high in the Gurian mountains at nearly 2,000 meters above sea level, Bakhmaro is one of Georgia's most iconic mountain resorts and a destination unlike anywhere else in the country. Famous for its unique climate, where cool mountain air blends with warm sea breezes from the Black Sea, Bakhmaro has long been cherished as a place of relaxation, wellness, and breathtaking natural beauty.

Surrounded by dense forests, alpine meadows, and panoramic mountain landscapes, Bakhmaro offers visitors an authentic escape into nature. During the summer months, the hills are covered with wildflowers, while the fresh air and peaceful atmosphere make it an ideal destination for families, hikers, photographers, and anyone seeking relief from the summer heat.

Adventure lovers will find countless opportunities to explore the surrounding mountains on foot, by horseback, or on scenic off-road routes leading to spectacular viewpoints. Traditional wooden cottages scattered across the hillsides preserve the timeless charm of this historic mountain resort, where life still follows the rhythm of nature.

One of Bakhmaro's most celebrated traditions is the annual horse racing festival, held every year on August 19 during the Feast of the Transfiguration. Riders from across western Georgia gather to compete in one of the country's highest-altitude horse races, while visitors enjoy traditional music, local cuisine, folk crafts, and the warm hospitality of Guria. The event marks the culmination of the summer season and has remained one of Georgia's most distinctive mountain festivals for generations.

Whether you come to hike through alpine landscapes, ride horses across mountain trails, witness the famous horse races, or simply enjoy the serenity of one of Georgia's most beautiful highland resorts, Bakhmaro promises an unforgettable experience far from the ordinary tourist routes.

nabeglavi.name: Nabeglavi
nabeglavi.description:
Hidden in the picturesque Gubazeuli River Valley, surrounded by lush forests and rolling mountains, Nabeglavi is one of Guria's most renowned natural treasures. While millions of people around the world recognize the name from the iconic bottle of Georgian mineral water, few have the opportunity to visit the place where it all begins. Located on the scenic road leading to Bakhmaro, Nabeglavi offers visitors much more than its famous spring it is a peaceful destination where nature, wellness, and authentic Georgian hospitality come together.

The story of Nabeglavi dates back to 1905, when the mineral spring was first discovered. Its unique composition and naturally carbonated water quickly gained recognition for its exceptional taste and beneficial mineral content. Today, the water is bottled according to international standards and exported to numerous countries, yet nothing compares to tasting it directly from its natural source in the heart of Guria.

Beyond its famous spring, Nabeglavi is a destination for travelers seeking relaxation and authentic nature. The fresh mountain air, crystal-clear Gubazeuli River, shaded picnic areas, and peaceful surroundings create the perfect setting for a short escape or a relaxing stop on the way to Bakhmaro. Visitors can enjoy scenic walks through the valley, discover nearby waterfalls, experience the tranquility of the Gurian countryside, and immerse themselves in one of Georgia's most beautiful natural landscapes.

For those exploring Guria, Nabeglavi is more than just a place to refill a bottle of mineral water. It is an opportunity to experience one of Georgia's most famous natural resources at its origin, surrounded by pristine landscapes that have attracted visitors for more than a century. Whether combined with a journey to Bakhmaro, a visit to local wineries, or an exploration of Guria's hidden villages, Nabeglavi is an essential stop on any itinerary through the region.

anaseuliTeaFactory.name: Anaseuli Tea Factory
anaseuliTeaFactory.description:
Nestled in the lush landscapes of Guria, Anaseuli Tea Factory is one of the most important landmarks in the history of Georgian tea. More than just a factory, it represents the birthplace of Georgia's scientific tea cultivation and the beginning of a tradition that once made the country one of the world's leading tea producers.

The history of tea in Guria dates back to the late 19th century, when the region's humid subtropical climate proved ideal for growing high-quality tea. By the early 20th century, Guria had become the heart of Georgia's tea industry, and Anaseuli emerged as its scientific and production center.

The historic factory, which began operating in the 1930s, still preserves much of its original equipment and production methods. Walking through its halls feels like stepping back in time, offering visitors a rare glimpse into the golden age of Georgian tea production. Here, traditional machinery, handcrafted techniques, and generations of experience continue to tell the story of a remarkable industry.

For decades, Georgian tea from Anaseuli was exported throughout the Soviet Union and beyond, becoming internationally known for its distinctive flavor and exceptional quality. Although tea production declined after the collapse of the Soviet Union, a new generation of passionate tea producers is now reviving this proud tradition.

Today, visitors can explore the historic factory, stroll through nearby tea plantations, learn about the fascinating journey from leaf to cup, and enjoy authentic tea tastings while discovering why Georgian tea is once again attracting international attention.

A visit to Anaseuli is not only a journey into the history of Georgian agriculture it is an opportunity to experience one of the country's most remarkable cultural revivals and understand why Guria remains the true home of Georgian tea.

ureki.name: Ureki
ureki.description:
Located on Georgia's beautiful Black Sea coast, Ureki is one of the country's most distinctive seaside destinations, renowned for its rare magnetic black sand. Rich in natural magnetite minerals, this unique beach is considered one of the very few places in the world where visitors can enjoy the therapeutic benefits of naturally magnetic sand while relaxing by the sea.

For decades, Ureki has been a popular wellness destination, attracting families, athletes, and travelers seeking both relaxation and health benefits. Many visitors believe that spending time on the warm black sand may help improve circulation, support the musculoskeletal system, and promote overall well-being. Combined with the fresh sea breeze and the peaceful coastal environment, Ureki offers a truly rejuvenating experience.

Unlike many busy seaside resorts, Ureki is known for its wide sandy beaches, shallow waters, and tranquil atmosphere, making it an excellent destination for families with children. The gently sloping shoreline allows safe swimming, while the surrounding pine forests create a pleasant microclimate and provide welcome shade during the hot summer months.

Beyond the beach itself, Ureki serves as an excellent starting point for exploring the hidden treasures of Guria. Visitors can easily combine a relaxing seaside holiday with wine tastings at boutique family wineries, tea plantation visits, authentic culinary experiences, and scenic journeys into the nearby mountains of Bakhmaro and Gomismta.

Whether you are looking for a unique wellness retreat, a family-friendly beach holiday, or a chance to discover the authentic culture of western Georgia, Ureki offers an unforgettable experience unlike anywhere else on the Black Sea coast.

wineCulture.name: Wine Culture of Guria
wineCulture.description:
For centuries, wine has been an inseparable part of everyday life in Guria. Although the region produces far less wine than Kakheti, it preserves one of Georgia's richest collections of endemic grape varieties and a deeply rooted family winemaking tradition.

Today, a new generation of passionate winemakers is bringing Gurian wine back to the spotlight. Small family wineries across the region are reviving forgotten grape varieties, restoring traditional qvevri winemaking methods, and producing exceptional natural wines that are increasingly recognized by wine enthusiasts around the world.

Unlike large commercial wineries, visiting Guria offers a much more personal experience. Guests are welcomed into family cellars, meet the winemakers themselves, taste wines produced in limited quantities, and enjoy authentic Gurian cuisine prepared with local ingredients.

Among Guria's most distinctive grape varieties are Chkhaveri, Sakmiela, Aladasturi, Jani, Mtevandidi, and Kamuri, each expressing the unique terroir and centuries-old viticultural heritage of the region.

askaneliEstate.name: Askaneli Estate
askaneliEstate.description:
One of Georgia's most internationally recognized wine producers, Askaneli combines centuries-old Georgian winemaking traditions with modern technology and innovation. Visitors can explore the winery, enjoy guided tastings of premium wines, chacha, and brandy, tour the production facilities, and learn the story behind one of Georgia's leading family-owned wine companies.

Location: Askana Village, Ozurgeti Municipality

rtoWinery.name: RTO Winery
rtoWinery.description:
A boutique family winery where guests can experience the authentic spirit of Gurian hospitality. Visitors are invited to taste handcrafted natural wines made from rare endemic grape varieties while learning directly from the family about traditional qvevri winemaking and the revival of Guria's wine culture.

Location: Jvartskhma Village, Chokhatauri Municipality

sharashidzeWinery.name: Sharashidze Family Winery
sharashidzeWinery.description:
This welcoming family winery offers visitors the opportunity to taste locally produced wines paired with traditional Gurian cuisine. Every visit is a personal experience, where guests can discover the stories, traditions, and hospitality that define the region.

Location: Ozurgeti Municipality

menabdeWinery.name: Menabde Winery
menabdeWinery.description:
Nestled in the scenic countryside of Guria, Menabde Winery specializes in handcrafted wines produced from indigenous grape varieties. Guests can enjoy intimate tastings, explore the vineyards, and experience authentic family hospitality surrounded by beautiful rural landscapes.

Location: Shemokmedi, Ozurgeti Municipality

babasMarani.name: Baba's Marani
babasMarani.description:
A true hidden gem for wine lovers, Baba's Marani offers an authentic family winery experience where tradition remains at the heart of every bottle. Visitors can discover small-batch wines produced using traditional Georgian methods, enjoy homemade Gurian cuisine, and experience genuine hospitality in a peaceful countryside setting.

Location: Goraberezhouli Village, Chokhatauri Municipality

armunji.name: Armunji
armunji.description:
More than just a winery, Armunji is an authentic agrotourism destination where guests can immerse themselves in the rural lifestyle of Guria. Surrounded by vineyards, orchards, and traditional farm life, visitors can enjoy local wines, seasonal cuisine prepared from fresh ingredients, and hands-on experiences that showcase the region's agricultural heritage. It is the perfect place to connect with nature, discover local traditions, and experience the true spirit of rural Georgia.

Location: Goraberezhouli Village, Chokhatauri Municipality

kalasFarm.name: Kala's Farm
kalasFarm.description:
Nestled in the peaceful countryside of Chokhatauri Municipality, Kala's Farm is one of Guria's most authentic agritourism destinations, where traditional farming meets modern artisan craftsmanship. Surrounded by green hills and fresh mountain air, the farm specializes in producing premium goat cheeses using fresh locally sourced milk and carefully refined production techniques.

Visitors are invited to explore every step of the cheesemaking process-from the farm and dairy workshop to the aging rooms where carefully crafted cheeses develop their unique character. Guided tours offer an opportunity to learn about sustainable farming practices, goat breeding, and the passion behind one of Guria's most distinctive artisan food producers.

The highlight of every visit is the tasting experience. Guests can sample a selection of handcrafted goat cheeses paired with seasonal local products, homemade preserves, fresh bread, and regional wines. More than just a tasting, Kala's Farm offers a genuine connection with local producers and an authentic glimpse into the agricultural traditions that continue to shape rural Guria.

Whether you are a food lover, a curious traveler, or simply looking to experience the authentic flavors of western Georgia, Kala's Farm is a memorable stop where quality, sustainability, and Gurian hospitality come together.

shekvetili.name: Shekvetili
shekvetili.description:
Located on the beautiful Black Sea coast of Guria, Shekvetili is one of Georgia's most modern and family-friendly seaside destinations. Surrounded by pine forests, sandy beaches, and fresh sea air, it offers a unique combination of nature, culture, recreation, and entertainment, making it an ideal destination for visitors of all ages.

One of Shekvetili's greatest attractions is its remarkable Dendrological Park a 60-hectare botanical paradise where visitors can explore hundreds of rare and exotic plant species collected from around the world. Giant sequoias, eucalyptus trees, magnolias, cedars, bamboo groves, and beautifully landscaped gardens create an extraordinary environment where nature flourishes. The park is also home to flamingos, exotic birds, and other wildlife, making it one of Georgia's most impressive green spaces.

Just a short walk away lies the Musicians Park, a unique open-air park where sculptures of legendary Georgian and international musicians come to life through music. As visitors stroll along the peaceful pathways, motion sensors play the most famous songs of each artist, creating an unforgettable atmosphere that combines art, music, and nature. Interactive installations, decorative ponds, sculptures, and beautifully maintained gardens make the park one of the region's most enjoyable places for relaxation.

For those looking to unwind, The Social Space offers a modern environment designed for relaxation, creativity, and connection with nature. Built with sustainability in mind, it combines comfortable outdoor seating, green surroundings, healthy food, and a peaceful atmosphere an ideal place to slow down after exploring the coast or nearby attractions.

Shekvetili is also home to the internationally renowned Black Sea Arena, one of the largest concert venues in the Caucasus. Throughout the year, the arena hosts world-famous musicians, festivals, and cultural events, making Shekvetili not only a seaside resort but also one of Georgia's leading cultural destinations.

Whether you're looking for a peaceful walk among exotic trees, an inspiring cultural experience, a relaxing day by the sea, or unforgettable family moments, Shekvetili perfectly combines the best of Guria's nature, culture, and modern recreation.

erketiMonastery.name: Erketi Monastery
erketiMonastery.description:
Hidden among the green hills of Chokhatauri Municipality, Erketi Monastery is one of Guria's oldest and most remarkable religious monuments. Dating back to the 9th-11th centuries, the monastery has served as an important spiritual center for generations and remains one of the region's most peaceful pilgrimage destinations.

Dedicated to the Archangels Michael and Gabriel, the monastery preserves centuries of Georgian Christian heritage within its ancient stone walls. Despite the many invasions and turbulent periods throughout Georgia's history, Erketi has safeguarded an impressive collection of religious treasures, including medieval frescoes, ancient manuscripts, sacred icons, and revered relics. It is one of the few places where visitors can experience an authentic atmosphere of devotion while discovering a remarkable chapter of Guria's spiritual history.

Surrounded by dense forests and peaceful countryside, the monastery offers more than historical significance. A natural spring in the churchyard has long been regarded by locals as having healing properties, while a nearby cave, once inhabited by monks seeking solitude and prayer, adds to the spiritual atmosphere of the site.

Today, Erketi Monastery welcomes both pilgrims and travelers searching for authentic cultural experiences beyond the traditional tourist routes. Its tranquil setting, remarkable history, and beautiful natural surroundings make it one of Guria's hidden treasures.

udabnoMonastery.name: Udabno Monastery
udabnoMonastery.description:
Perched on the steep slopes of Amaghleba Mountain in Chokhatauri Municipality, Udabno Monastery of St. John the Baptist is one of the oldest and most extraordinary monastic sites in western Georgia. Despite its name, which means "desert" in Georgian, the monastery is surrounded by dense forests, natural springs, and breathtaking mountain scenery. Here, the word Udabno refers not to a barren landscape, but to the secluded life of monks who sought silence, prayer, and spiritual devotion far from the outside world.

The heart of the monastery is a remarkable 6th-century rock-hewn church, partially carved directly into the cliff. It is considered one of the oldest surviving cave churches in western Georgia and remains a rare example of early Georgian Christian architecture. Nearby caves once served as chapels and monastic cells, preserving the atmosphere of one of Guria's earliest spiritual communities.

For centuries, Udabno was not only a place of prayer but also an important center of education and manuscript production. Monks copied religious texts, translated theological works, and maintained a renowned library. Among its greatest treasures was the "Udabno Mravaltavi", a remarkable 9th-century manuscript regarded as one of the most valuable works of medieval Georgian literature. Although many priceless manuscripts and icons were lost during the Soviet era, the monastery remains a powerful symbol of Georgia's cultural and spiritual resilience.

Today, the restored St. John the Baptist Men's Monastery continues its centuries-old monastic tradition. Visitors are rewarded not only with a profound sense of peace but also with spectacular panoramic views over southern Guria, making Udabno one of the region's most inspiring pilgrimage and cultural destinations.

zhgentiSisters.name: Zhgenti Sisters
zhgentiSisters.description:
Hidden among the rolling green hills of Melekeduri Village, the Zhgenti Sisters' Tea Plantation offers one of Guria's most authentic and personal tea experiences. Run by sisters Lana and Inga Zhgenti, this family estate has become a symbol of the revival of Georgian tea culture, welcoming visitors to discover the traditions, flavours, and warm hospitality of rural Guria.

Guests are invited to walk through beautiful tea plantations, learn how tea leaves are carefully hand-picked, and discover every stage of traditional tea production from freshly harvested leaves to a perfectly brewed cup. The experience continues with a guided tasting of handcrafted Gurian teas, where every variety tells the story of the region's rich tea heritage.

But what truly makes this place special is its atmosphere. Visitors are welcomed into the family's home, where tea is shared alongside homemade Gurian delicacies, local stories, and genuine conversations. Whether relaxing on the terrace overlooking the valley, joining the seasonal tea harvest, or simply enjoying the peaceful countryside, guests experience the kind of authentic hospitality that cannot be found in traditional tourist attractions.

The Zhgenti Sisters have transformed their family plantation into a destination where culture, nature, and community come together. It is not just a tea tasting it is an opportunity to connect with the people who are bringing Georgian tea back to life, one leaf at a time

With Tour Provider Georgia, you can experience all of this firsthand. Join the Zhgenti Sisters for seasonal tea picking, discover the secrets of traditional tea-making, enjoy a guided tea tasting, and spend unforgettable moments sharing homemade Gurian cuisine, local stories, and genuine hospitality.

tsitsinatela.name: Tsitsinatela
tsitsinatela.description:
Located near Shekvetili on the Black Sea coast, Tsitsinatela is one of Georgia's largest and most popular amusement parks. Open during the summer season, it offers dozens of attractions for visitors of all ages, making it a favourite destination for families, groups of friends, and anyone looking for excitement after a relaxing day by the sea.

From thrilling roller coasters and adrenaline-filled rides to children's attractions, Ferris wheels, games, restaurants, and evening entertainment, Tsitsinatela creates a lively atmosphere that attracts thousands of visitors every year. Beautifully illuminated after sunset, the park becomes one of the region's most vibrant nightlife attractions, combining fun, music, and unforgettable summer memories.

Whether you're travelling with children or simply looking for an entertaining evening on Georgia's Black Sea coast, Tsitsinatela is the perfect place to add excitement to your Guria journey.

jumatiMonastery.name: Jumati Monastery
jumatiMonastery.description:
Perched on a forested hill overlooking the beautiful landscapes of Guria, Jumati Monastery is one of the region's most important religious and cultural landmarks. Founded between the 10th and 11th centuries, the monastery was dedicated to the Archangels Michael and Gabriel and became one of medieval Georgia's most influential spiritual, educational, and artistic centers.

For centuries, Jumati was renowned not only as a place of worship but also as a guardian of priceless Georgian treasures. The monastery housed an extraordinary collection of illuminated manuscripts, precious icons, liturgical objects, and goldsmith masterpieces, many of which are now preserved in museums across Georgia. Among its most celebrated treasures was the magnificent Jumati Triptych, regarded as one of the finest examples of medieval Georgian ecclesiastical art.

Surrounded by lush forests and peaceful mountain scenery, the monastery offers visitors a unique combination of history, spirituality, and breathtaking nature. Walking through its ancient grounds, guests can admire traditional Georgian architecture while enjoying panoramic views over the valleys of Guria. The tranquil atmosphere makes Jumati an ideal destination for those seeking both cultural discovery and peaceful reflection.

Today, Jumati Monastery remains one of Guria's most treasured historical monuments, attracting pilgrims, history enthusiasts, and travelers eager to explore the region's rich cultural heritage beyond the well-known tourist routes.

adjara.name: Adjara
adjara.lead: Adjara is one of Georgia's most distinctive and diverse regions, where the Black Sea coastline, lush green mountains, breathtaking waterfalls, rivers, and centuries-old traditions come together to create a truly unique world.
adjara.p1: It is a place where travellers can experience remarkable contrasts within a single day beginning the morning with the tranquillity of the seaside, and only a few hours later finding themselves surrounded by misty mountains, ancient villages, and landscapes where traditional ways of life have been preserved for generations.
adjara.p2: Adjara is far more than Batumi and its coastline. The true character of the region reveals itself when visitors leave the shore and journey towards mountainous Adjara through verdant valleys, charming villages, and remote places where nature and human traditions exist in perfect harmony.
adjara.p3:
Here, travellers encounter mountain communities where ancestral customs are still carefully preserved, alongside authentic local cuisine, a unique culture of hospitality, and a peaceful rhythm of life that has remained unchanged for centuries.

The natural diversity of Adjara is truly remarkable. Ancient Colchian forests, protected areas, cascading waterfalls, mountain rivers, and breathtaking landscapes create an ideal environment for those seeking a deeper connection with nature and wishing to discover the lesser-known treasures of Georgia.

The region is also renowned for its exceptional cultural heritage. In Adjara, coastal and mountain cultures meet, creating a unique blend of ancient traditions, Georgian hospitality, and a distinctive local way of life.

Travelling through Adjara is an opportunity to discover Georgia in many different colors  the deep blue of the sea, the endless green of the mountains, the tranquillity of traditional villages, and the warmth of its people.

This is a region where every road tells a story, every village preserves its own traditions, and every visit becomes an authentic Georgian experience.

Discover Adjara a place where the sea meets the mountains, nature embraces culture, and traditions continue to live.

batumi.name: Batumi
batumi.description:
The true uniqueness of Batumi lies in its remarkable contrast. It is a city that respects its centuries-old heritage, preserves the traces of its past, and at the same time continues to evolve, transform, and confidently move towards the future.

Today, Batumi is one of Georgia's most vibrant and dynamic cities a place where the Black Sea coastline, modern architecture, rich history, and influences of different cultures come together to create a truly distinctive atmosphere.

However, the authentic character of Batumi cannot be understood through its modern appearance alone. This is a city that has experienced countless transformations throughout centuries while continuously remaining a meeting point of different civilizations, peoples, and cultures.

Since ancient times, Batumi's strategic location on the Black Sea coast has given it great importance. Its position turned the city into a significant maritime and trading centre, where different cultures and civilizations crossed paths and contributed to the unique diversity that defines Batumi today.

In the 19th century, Batumi entered a period of major transformation, especially after gaining recognition as a free port a status known as Porto Franco. This era became a turning point in the city's economic and cultural development. Trade expanded, new architectural styles appeared, infrastructure developed, and Batumi gradually grew into a port of international significance.

These historical processes shaped Batumi's multicultural identity. Throughout different periods, the city became home to Georgians, Greeks, Armenians, Jews, Russians, Europeans, and representatives of many other communities. Each group left its mark on Batumi's architecture, traditions, cuisine, and everyday life, creating the diverse cultural character that remains visible today.

Modern Batumi is a place where the past and the present exist side by side. Walking through the streets of Old Batumi, visitors can experience the atmosphere of 19th-century Europe historic buildings, charming courtyards, and distinctive architectural details. Yet only a few steps away, they encounter a contemporary city with its famous seaside boulevard, modern skyline, high-rise buildings, and vibrant coastal lifestyle.

For visitors, Batumi is much more than a seaside destination. It is a city where you can stroll along the Black Sea promenade, explore historic neighbourhoods, taste authentic Adjara cuisine, discover local traditions, and experience the unique atmosphere that has been shaped over centuries.

khelvachauri.name: Khelvachauri
khelvachauri.description:
Just a few minutes away from Batumi begins a different side of Adjara a place where the rhythm of the city gradually fades and travellers discover a quieter, greener, and more authentic atmosphere.

Khelvachauri is one of Adjara's distinctive municipalities, combining breathtaking natural landscapes, forest-covered valleys, mountain rivers, historical sites, and a traditional way of life that has preserved its authentic character through generations.

Many visitors discover Adjara through its famous seaside destinations, yet the true spirit of the region can often be found in places like Khelvachauri  where nature, culture, and everyday local life exist together in perfect harmony.

The uniqueness of Khelvachauri lies in its diversity. Within a short distance, travellers can discover the peaceful beauty of green valleys, the crystal-clear waters of mountain rivers, impressive waterfalls, and traditional villages where hospitality and customs continue to be passed from one generation to the next.

Among the natural treasures of the region, the Kapnistavi Waterfalls stand out as a hidden gem of exceptional beauty. Surrounded by forests and untouched nature, this peaceful destination reveals a more intimate and authentic side of Adjara. The sound of mountain streams, the fresh air, and the tranquillity of the surrounding landscape create an experience for those seeking places beyond the usual tourist routes.

The cultural identity of Khelvachauri is enriched by the unique Borjgalo Museum, a place where Adjara's traditional lifestyle, crafts, art, and ancestral knowledge come to life. More than a collection of historical exhibits, the museum offers visitors a deeper understanding of local heritage, traditional values, and the cultural roots that continue to shape the region today.

A journey through Khelvachauri offers an opportunity to discover a side of Adjara that often remains beyond standard travel itineraries. Here, visitors encounter not only beautiful landscapes but also local stories, traditions, and the genuine atmosphere that makes every region of Georgia unique.

Places like Khelvachauri transform a simple excursion into a meaningful discovery an opportunity to connect with nature, history, and the people who preserve these traditions.

Khelvachauri a place where, just a few kilometres from Batumi, another Georgia begins: greener, quieter, and more authentic, where natural beauty and centuries-old traditions come together to create a truly unforgettable experience.

keda.name: Keda
keda.description:
Keda is one of Adjara's most distinctive municipalities, where nature, history, wine culture, and ancient traditions come together to create a truly unique experience. It is a place where travellers discover not only breathtaking landscapes but also the stories and people who have shaped the identity of this region over centuries.

The character of Keda has been formed through the deep connection between mountains, rivers, and local communities. Within the municipality, two important rivers Adjaristskali and Chorokhi meet, creating a place of both geographical and historical significance. Throughout history, such fertile landscapes provided favourable conditions for settlement, agriculture, and the development of viticulture.

Keda is particularly renowned for its ancient winemaking traditions. The region's unique climate influenced by both the Black Sea and the mountains, with a humid environment and fertile soils has created ideal conditions for grape cultivation and wine production for centuries.
